key_insight: Reinforcement learning improved an LLM’s interactive colon cancer treatment planning using patient-specific rewards derived from clinical decision processes.
clinical_relevance: This study explores first-line treatment planning—not drug discovery—and does not establish clinical safety or patient benefit.
method: Model planning as sequential information gathering under partial observability.
Construct process-aware rewards from real-world clinical records.
Train Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with GRPO and GDPO reinforcement learning.
evidence_signal: In the study’s interactive evaluation, GDPO increased Mean@3 scalar clinical reward by 79.60% over base Llama and exceeded GPT-5.2 by 18.82%, while query counts decreased during training.
watch_item: Higher reward scores do not establish better patient outcomes; prospective clinical validation is needed.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning In Partially Verifiable Environments for Colon Cancer Treatment Planning
